read.sections.0.text.back: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and love. Hearing words you know can help you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. For example, in Paraguay, many people speak Spanish and Guaraní. Someone who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. A person's level of English does not show how clever they are. It also does not show whether their ideas are important.
read.sections.0.text.source: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing a word you know can help you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. In Paraguay, for example, many people speak both Spanish and Guaraní. Someone who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English does not show how clever they are. It does not show whether their ideas matter.

read.sections.1.text.back: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign language, which is a complete language with its own grammar. The United Nations states that there are more than 300 sign languages in the world. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The pictograms on the notice show food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand its main message. But pictures cannot give every detail, such as what needs to be brought. Volunteers who can translate still help.

read.sections.2.text.back: Languages change over time. Languages also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word “coffee” has travelled far. It started as the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, then reached English. Many languages are also related. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because those languages developed from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another language. Every language carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.
read.sections.2.text.source: Languages change over time. They also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word “coffee” travelled a long way. It started as the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and then it reached English. Many languages are also related. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because they grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another. Each one carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Languages change over time. Languages take words from other languages. Look at the word “coffee”. It started in Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian, and then into English. Some languages are like cousins. These languages come from one old language. So they are all in one language family. English, Hindi and Persian are in one family. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in another family. No language is the best. Every language keeps the stories of the people who speak it.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Languages change over time. They take words from each other. Look at the word “coffee”. It began in Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian. Then it came into English. Some languages are like cousins. They grew from one old language. So they are in one language family. English, Hindi and Persian are in one. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in a different one. No language is the best. Each one holds the stories of the people who speak it.

write.example.back: I would add the notice in two or three languages that visitors use. This helps because more people can read it in a language they know. I would also put a helper at the door who can translate. This helps people ask questions, such as what needs to be brought. One limitation is that a written notice cannot help people who do not read. The pictures and the helper can help with that. This shows that using more than one way to share a message helps more people feel welcome.

watch.summary.back: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language split up and moved to different places. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way they spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. Over time, one language became several languages. Languages that developed from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, such as numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts check them carefully. It is hard to say where one language ends and another language begins. Therefore, different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with one idea: a language that sounds new to you might be related to a language you know.
watch.summary.source: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language moved apart. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way it spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. In time, one language became several languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts check them with care. It can be hard to say where one language ends and another begins. So different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with an idea: a language that sounds new to you may be related to one you know.
